about: The epistola of the formulary “5th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Dearly beloved: Be all of one mind in prayer, sympathetic, lovers of the brotherhood, merciful, modest, humble; not returning evil for evil, nor curse for curse, but on the contrary blessing, because to this you have been called, so that you may possess a blessing as an inheritance. For whoever wishes to love life and to see good days must curb his tongue from evil and keep his lips from speaking deceit. Let him turn aside from evil and do what is good; let him seek peace and follow it. For the Lord’s eyes are on the just, and to their prayers His ears are turned; but the Lord’s face is on those who do evil. And who is there that would harm you, if you have been zealous for the good? Yet even if you suffer something on account of justice, you are blessed. And have no fear of their fear, nor be disturbed. Rather, in your hearts sanctify the Lord Christ.

ex.w100: The adjective is the predicate of an understood subject, the readers of the letter, with the verb left out: “[you are] blessed”.
